label: input r late in the original phase of a sequence that starts with q
explanation: Fires almost only in sequences whose first original token is q (95% of activation mass; 28x lift). Within those, it fires mostly when the input is r (78% of mass, 22x lift) at original positions 4-8, usually the last 1-3 tokens before <DEL>. It never fires at t<4 or during the copy phase. There is a weak secondary activation at the <DEL> step (5% of mass, where q is the next output) and on other late original tokens in q-initial sequences. The strongest examples also have y (often with h or u) earlier in the prefix: requiring y raises precision to about 0.57 but cuts recall sharply. Precision of the main predicate is only about 0.23, because many q...r sequences without those prefix tokens stay silent. So the explanation captures most of the mass but not what gates it.
